topology: PC1 → R1 → R2 → SRV1. R1 summarizes 192.168.32.0/22 toward R2. R2 has a connected 192.168.32.0/24 service LAN and a default back to R1. Unused 192.168.35.10 initially loops through the summary/default pair; R2 must add the matching /22 Null0 discard guard with distance250.
implemented: Fourth CCNP ENARSI Layer3 lab; accessible section counts now show four. Includes independent practice/completed variants, four-row addressing/role plan, staged guide, working reference commands and current-site domain/path/query permalinks. All existing categories and39 ENCOR entries remain available.

Twelve tasks combine four live configuration/state/save goals with eight historical observations. Practice starts0/12; reference starts4/12 without traffic or fabricated incidents. Earned observations persist through export/import, while live forwarding, topology health and saved state revoke on drift.

Initial proof correlates three distinct client echo requests: each revisits both routers, produces a TTL1 discard and returns a parent-linked ICMP Type11 Code0 error to PC1. Six-hop Windows trace independently shows alternating routers. Queries, unrelated packets and fewer than three loop probes cannot earn the loop task.

The configured Null0 /22 guard terminates three new unused-summary requests at R2 without hairpin forwarding or TTL expiry. The connected /24 continues to deliver three real service replies, demonstrating prefix length precedence separately from administrative distance.

Three controlled incidents require genuine fault evidence followed by fresh repaired traffic: R2 service interface shutdown withdraws its connected /24 and triggers safe discard; a wrong more-specific /24 via R1 overrides the guard after connected withdrawal and causes actual TTL-expiring loops; later removal of the guard recreates the original unused-summary loop, followed by restored discard and service delivery.

The more-specific repair requires removing the bad static route as well as restoring the interface; merely hiding it behind the connected route does not pass health or the repair task. Server power loss and interface toggles without observed discard do not count as the prescribed withdrawal incident.

HTTP success requires a complete real200 response with the expected page, matching server transaction and routed request. Saved goals compare both routers running and startup configuration. Normal simulator notifications capture synchronous CLI results when the guide is closed; per-attempt ownership resets with a new lab.

No simulation engine, global UI, terminal style, node artwork or networking behavior changed. The lab uses existing static forwarding, CEF lookup, TTL handling, ICMP errors, traceroute and HTTP implementation.
scope: IPv4 IOS summary/default forwarding-loop prevention and longest-prefix failure handling. Does not claim CML validation for this new lab or configure mutual redistribution, EIGRP feasible successors, RIP split horizon, BGP AS-path loop prevention, IPv6 or NX-OS.
